back: The money needed to set up a business before it earns revenue: premises, equipment, first stock and early expenses.
The finance needed for day-to-day running: wages, bills and stock paid for before customers pay.
Short-term (up to about a year): wages, stock, bills. Long-term: machinery, vehicles, buildings. Match the finance to the life of the asset.
Profit = revenue - costs for a period. Cash = money actually received and paid. Credit sales raise profit before they raise cash.
Closing balance = opening balance + cash received - cash paid. A negative result is an overdraft.
A legal process for an individual (such as a sole trader) who cannot pay their debts; assets are used to repay creditors.
A company is closed down and its assets are sold to pay creditors.
An administrator takes control of an insolvent company to rescue it or sell it as a going concern, with temporary protection from creditors.
Cash shortage, too little start-up capital, over-expansion, bad debts and falling sales.
